feedback.end: An earthquake happens when tectonic plates rub or push against one another and cause the ground to shake. Earthquakes occur almost constantly around the world, but most are so small that they can’t be felt.

atoms.b: The Earth’s crust is split up into different pieces called tectonic ((++plates spoons)). The point where these plates meet is called a plate ((++boundary dictionary)).
These plates are constantly moving in different directions. Plates that slide past each other create ((++friction gravity)), and plates that ((++push_into help)) each other build pressure.
After a build up of ((water ++friction)) or pressure, a large amount of energy is suddenly released as an earthquake.

atoms.text: Every earthquake has a focus. This is the place where the earthquake starts inside the Earth’s crust. They also have an epicentre, which is the point on the Earth’s surface directly above the focus.
Earthquakes also have foreshocks, which are smaller earthquakes that come before the main earthquake in the same location. Aftershocks are similar, but they occur after the mainshock.
